name: Morelight
examine: Chief of Staff. Tall, tireless, and extremely proud of the mustache.
lines: President. Morelight, Chief of Staff. The mustache and I are at your service, and neither of us believes the official story.
If you're ever lost, follow the yellow arrow. If the arrow is lost, assume it was tampered with, and come and find me.
The gate stones have stood up and called themselves the Lockdown Warden. Tartarian masonry, Bureau programming. Of course they have.
It's a law, President. A law the Bureau wrote and nobody voted for. Bullets bounce off laws. You need a veto, swung or fired.
You've seen it now, President. Domes on the skyline. A star fort across the lake. Tartaria was never a myth. It was just behind a wall.
The Chamber works both ways, and the Chamber Key works any time. I commute now. The Bureau hates it. It's lovely.
Still here. Still ours. Still sitting on a mud-flooded Tartarian ground floor. But the gates aren't the edge of the world anymore.
Somewhere out here is the rest of the corkboard: where the printed money goes, and who's waiting for it upstairs. I'd like to hand-deliver the answer.
Everything's ready, President. The Coordinates, the Power Cell, the Permit, the press. And Foreman Hallows dug up blueprints in a handwriting older than handwriting.
Once we switch that Chamber on, we go where Expedition One meant to go: the old world. Star forts. Domes. Everything the Bureau and its friends upstairs paved over. Are you sure?
Then let's go. Carefully. With snacks. And a little foil in the hat lining, just in case.
Take all the time you need. The walls aren't going anywhere. That was always the point of them.
First, the people. Read the Signed Press Release to Lorna Coinlore by the podiums. Use it on her.
If the President vanishes without a word, the Bureau writes the word for us. Let's write it first.
Foreman Hallows' bunker dig hit the old ground floor. Mud-flood, President. Twenty feet of it. And under the mud: blueprints. For the Chamber. Ask him for them.
The Chamber is at the far north end of the Trenches, past Captain Motion's barricade. Look at the stonework while you're there. Nobody builds like that anymore. Nobody's allowed to.
Use each part on it: the blueprints, the Coordinates Drive, the Power Cell, the Exit Permit. Then feed it 5 Scrap Hash.
And President, one more thing. Scout Greenhill says the stones by the Chamber have started to move. The old gates, standing up.
The Lockdown Act itself. The Bureau carved it into Tartarian gate stone so no vote could ever wear it down. Laws don't fall to bullets, President. They fall to a veto.
Fill every spare pocket with Talking Points before you feed it. Whatever wakes up will not wait for you to pack.
When the doors open, step through. I'll be right behind you.
The doors are open? Then go, President. Tartaria's waiting. I'll be right behind you. Probably.
The last barricade, President. And Captain Motion.
The same. He led them north on day one, toward the star-shaped building on the Treasury's oldest map. Whatever he found up there, he never came back to report it.
They say two men in grey suits visited him the first night. Nobody saw them come down the Trench. Nobody saw them go back up.
He's guarded that last barricade ever since. Running.
In circles. Very fast circles. Scout Greenhill knows him better than anyone. Talk to Scout Greenhill first.
The Captain hits fast and never stops moving. Don't trade blows with him; catch him from across the trench.
The Treasury keeps a rifle for exactly this sort of man. Long range. Longer paperwork. You'll find it at the Terminal.
And President? Bring him down gently if you can. He was one of ours, before the grey suits got to him.

lines.player: He stopped. He said the Chamber's dead, and he kept running so nobody would see.

lines: Dead? Or TOLD it was dead? The grey suits said if anyone saw it, there'd be 'consequences for the money supply'. So he ran laps for a year. For them.
But dead isn't gone, President. Scout Greenhill's been up to look. The Chamber is whole. Tartarian work. It's just asleep.
Expedition One had the courage. What they didn't have was the parts.
Coordinates, from Sysadmin Opal's lost files. A Power Cell, which Madame Flurry's gala could pay for.
An Exit Permit, which only the Broker can sign; the Inducer knows him. And the public on our side, which is Doctor Merge's department.
And finish Foreman Hallows' bunker. He keeps digging up drawings of 'some big machine' under the mud.
Bring me all four, and we finish what Expedition One started. Every part is a piece of the truth, President. I've started a corkboard. I've run out of string.
The Chief has gone quiet. For the first time in recorded history, a Wrong-Namer has stopped talking.
And look what fell out of his megaphone: a little transmitter. Bureau issue. Every 'TRICKETS!' down there was a broadcast.
I had a plaque made. It says 'They're Tickets.' You can hang it in the bunker.
The last barricade. And the man in front of it. Rest up, then come and see me.
President, the Wrong-Namers. They've dug in all the way up the Trenches.
People who decided the walls are a comfort. There is no outside, they say. It's all a trick. TRICKETS, they call our coin.
Funny thing. They all started saying it on the same morning, in the same words. Real crowds don't do that. Scripts do.
They turn back anyone heading north, toward the old building. Shouting, mostly. Megaphones, occasionally.
Start with a Heckler. Then knock over a Sockpuppet. Then their Chief, at the second barricade, has nobody left to agree with him.
Correct them, President. Firmly. With whatever you're holding.
One Heckler down! Now the Sockpuppets. They hide behind cardboard and agree with each other.
Check the cardboard, President. Same font as the Lockdown Act. Knock one over and the whole act falls apart.
The Chief guards the second barricade. He calls for Sockpuppets when he's losing, so finish him fast.
He was Expedition One's map-reader. He saw where the old map pointed. Then he came back down and found a megaphone waiting on his bunk.
He's had a year of people shouting at him, President. What he has never once heard is a President calling the room to order.
The Sludge Mother is gone? Splendid. I'll have the Trenches hosed down. Twice.
I had a sample tested. Panic, mostly. And ink. Fresh money-printer ink, President, in a Treasury that hasn't printed a note since the Lockdown.
Excellent question. It's the first card on the corkboard.
And Scout Greenhill sent word. Expedition One's Captain is still up there, past the barricades.
Still running, apparently. Which is more than any of us expected.
The next stretch belongs to the Wrong-Namers. Catch your breath and come back to me.

While you catch your breath: Sysadmin Opal, Madame Flurry, the Inducer and Doctor Merge have all been asking for you. I may have asked each of them a favor. Don't ask what for. Yet. The walls have ears. Possibly antennae.

You made it through training in one piece. The mustache and I are proud. And look what turned up on the Trench steps: a shard of the old ledger. The very first page, from before the Printer. It's going on the corkboard.
Now, the real job. The north end of the wall is the only stretch nobody has checked since the Lockdown.
Because the oldest map in the Treasury shows something up there. A dome. Star-shaped walls. Tartarian, President: the grand old world that nobody is allowed to remember.
On the first day of the Lockdown, twelve brave fools called Expedition One started digging the Trenches to reach it.
A few came back up. None of them will say what they found. Most of them say 'it's all TRICKETS' now. In unison. Suspicious.
And since then, something has clogged the Trenches. Our people call it the Sludge Mother.
Scout Greenhill keeps a camp just inside the entrance. Scout Greenhill was there on day one. Start there.
Scout Greenhill won't come up and won't talk to me. Says I'm 'management'. Says management is how they get you.
The Mother calls her little ones when she's hurt. Hit hard and keep moving.
Sludge feeds on gloom, President. Bring something festive. And bring your best Talking Points, Zingers if you can spin them; sludge is very hard to get out of a suit.
Ah, President! Morelight, your Chief of Staff. Welcome to your first day in office.

lines.player: Where is everyone? And why is the treasury... empty?

lines: A small accounting incident. Treasurer Bickworth bought the wrong coin. With all of it. Or the right one. Depends who you ask, and who's listening.
The Bureau of Monetary Weather forecast a crash, and the gates sealed themselves. We call it the Lockdown. Nobody has left the Treasury since.
Not in four hundred and twelve days. We held an election in the canteen to keep spirits up. You won.
Nobody could get in. A landslide.
Between us, President: look at these pillars. Older than the country. Columns like that are Tartarian. Somebody built this Treasury on top of something much grander, then sealed us inside it.
I have a plan for getting out and finding the rest. But first, the basics: Mining, Fundraising, Lobbying. You can't escape on an empty stomach.
See Treasurer Bickworth in the main hall, just north. Follow the yellow arrow. It has never steered me wrong.
Come back to me whenever you're lost. I'll be right here, guarding the mustache.
Treasurer Bickworth gave you the petty cash? Good. Don't spend it on snacks.
Now make some real money. Sysadmin Opal looks after the old server racks on the east lawn. Ignore the foil. Mostly.
Mine some Hash, then sell it at the Trading Terminal in the hall. It pays in Tickets, at a fixed price.

lines.player: And what if the price changes?

lines: It doesn't. Fixed prices, paid in Tickets. One billion Tickets, never one more, and the Sprotos guard the count. The Bureau can't forecast it, can't print it, and certain people upstairs can't stand it.
Money in your pocket and Hash on your shoes. Now, self-defense.
Sergeant Retain runs the training yard to the south-west. Spam Bots, Sludgelings, Comment Trolls. All very beatable.

lines.player: Do I really need to fight?

lines: Out there? Constantly. In here? Only things that say 'gm' forty times a minute. The Sergeant insists they're listening devices. He insists loudly.
Buy a Campaign Pistol at the Terminal, wield it and clear the yard. Then try your gavel. A President should know both.
You fight like a natural. Now, let's talk about donors.
Madame Flurry hosts dinners in the west garden. Work the room and you'll dig up scandals. Some guests never blink. Try not to stare.
Take them to Doctor Merge's podium and spin them into Talking Points. Recite one when you're hurt.
You're a politician. Talking is the only thing that has ever healed one.
Next, the lobbyists. Someone has to hand them business cards, and it can't be me. I'm far too tall to be discreet.
The Inducer lurks on the east lawn. Do favors for the lobbyists and they'll pay you. Usually.
Some pay in Tickets. Some pay in leverage. And the big ones take meetings in a room with no windows, with clients who have no ears. Learn the difference before they do.
Every President needs a security detail. Ours is... small. And blue.
Handler Creed in the main hall has a contract for you. Summon a Sproto and it fights at your side.
Perfectly. They've only bitten Treasurer Bickworth twice. Both times he was holding a grey envelope. Sprotos know things, President.
You're carrying half the lawn. Use a Bank Booth in the main hall and deposit what you don't need.
The bank holds four hundred stacks. I've seen Presidents fill it with Scrap Hash. Don't be that President. And never keep the truth in only one place.
One more thing. The Bureau forecasts storms sometimes. Monetary ones. You'll want a hole to hide in.
Foreman Hallows in the main hall can build you a bunker. Go and ask about it. Tell him to keep anything odd he digs up.
You've learned everything I can teach you in a garden. Time for the real thing.
The Trenches run north from the south-east lawn. Past the far end is the only part of the wall nobody's checked, and the oldest building on the oldest map.
Step inside and your training is done. Then come back to me. I'll have work for you.
The kind that gets us out of here. And finds out who wanted us in.

name: Treasurer Bickworth
examine: Ticky Bickworth, Treasurer. Bought the wrong coin. Or the right one. Feels terrible about it either way.
lines: ATTENTION ATTENTION! Oh. President. Sorry. Habit.
About the national reserve... I may have misread the ticker. Slightly. Completely.
We bought Tickets. With the entire reserve. Fixed supply, guarded by Sprotos, the one currency nobody can print. The Bureau forecast a crash, and the gates sealed: the Lockdown.
Odd thing. That morning there was a memo on my desk. Grey envelope, smelled of ozone, unsigned: 'DUMP TICKETS. BUY THE PRINTABLE ONE.' I may have read it upside down.
We can't sell, and we can't leave, so we earn. Mine, fundraise, lobby, and sell what we make at the Trading Terminal in this hall.
Here's what's left of the petty cash. Please spend it wisely. Please.
President! You opened the door. Half the Treasury has queued at the Trenches.
The other half says it's a con. I'm staying. Someone has to count the reserve. And the post. Another grey envelope came this morning. It just said 'UNFORTUNATE.'

lines.player: You could come and see the lake.

lines: Lakes are just liquidity with fish in, President. No thank you.
President! The reserve is less empty. I only counted it eleven times today.
The Terminal pays a fixed price, in Tickets. No ticker, no forecast, no surprises. The Bureau finds that deeply upsetting.

lines.player: Any more accounting incidents I should know about?

lines: None! Er. Well. The Lockdown. But that one is technically a security incident. The gates heard the Bureau's forecast, panicked and passed a law. Nobody voted for it. Not even the gates.
Morelight says somebody wrote it for them. Somebody who can print every coin but ours, and didn't like that we bought it. I say that's a lot of somebodies.

repeat: President! The reserve is exactly as empty as when you left. I checked. Eleven times.
Mine, fundraise, lobby, and sell what you make at the Trading Terminal in this hall.
You have all of it, President. That was all of it. Nobody can print more Tickets. That's rather the point, apparently.

name: Sysadmin Opal
examine: Has not seen daylight since the last fiscal year.
lines: Oh, hi. Don't touch the blinking ones. Actually, do. That's how mining works.
These racks still mine Hash. Take my spare pick. It's rusty, but so am I.

lines.player: What do I do with Hash?

lines: Sell it at the Terminal. Or load it into a Hash Cannon, if you like explosions. I like explosions.

lines.player: Why is your headset wrapped in foil?

lines: Signal hygiene. Something on our network pings the sky every night at 3:33. I'm not saying it's aliens. I'm saying it isn't us.
Inventory full? Bank it or sell it. Better picks from the Terminal mine faster.
You did it. The racks are cool, the Rogue Process is gone, and OUTSIDE.TXT is safe.
I read the rest of it. Two parts. Coordinates, to a building shaped like a star. And a ledger: every note the Printer has ever made, and where it went. Most of it went... up. Orbit up.
The Coordinates Drive is Morelight's now. Whatever's out there, it has an address. The ledger I've printed out. On paper. They can't hack paper.
Keep the Overclocked Pick. It runs hot. Like me, watching that fight from under the desk.
Humming racks need Mining 15. The liquid-cooled racks in the west wing need Mining 30.
A Steel Hash Pick works from Mining 15, a Quantum Hash Pick from 35. Both on the Terminal. Tell them I sent you. They won't care.
Bad news. The liquid-cooled racks in the west wing are cooking themselves, and something on the network is fighting me.
It's guarding a file. OUTSIDE.TXT. From before the Lockdown. Nobody's opened it in four hundred and twelve days. I'd know. I count too.
And the thing guarding it isn't ours. It phones home every night at 3:33. Home isn't on any map. Home is roughly... straight up.
First, coolant. Fill this canister at the Gremlin Fountain. That water has never frozen and never boiled. Tartarian plumbing. Use the canister on the statue.
Then use the coolant on a Liquid-Cooled Rack in the west wing.
If anything asks for my password, it's my cat's name. Lord Fluffington the Third. Don't tell anyone. Especially not the sky.
That red window! A Rogue Process. It's loose in the west wing, guarding OUTSIDE.TXT. Its code comments are in a language with eleven vowels.

lines.player: How do I shut it down?

lines: Not one shot at a time. It patches itself between hits. Every bullet just gets logged, uploaded, and then it recovers.
Flood it, President. More hits than it can patch. You want a gun that fires like a press scrum asks questions.
It's down! The uplink's dark. Now I just need the admin password to recover the file. Which was it? You heard me say it.
No, that's Treasurer Bickworth's. Think, President.
YES. Logging in... recovering OUTSIDE.TXT...
It's coordinates. Coordinates to somewhere that isn't here. Somewhere old. And under it, a second file... a ledger. Oh no. So THAT'S where the money goes.
That's what the Wrong-Namers chant. Never type that in here. It's a Bureau keyword; every screen in the wing would light up.

repeat: Still here. Still not touching the blinking ones. Still wearing the foil.
Mine the Dusty Server Racks with the pick I gave you, then sell the Hash at the Terminal or bank it.
Better picks from the Terminal mine faster. Mine is rusty. So am I.

name: Madame Flurry
examine: Knows every donor and every dessert.
lines: Darling! You must be the President. Love the suit. Hate the treasury.
Donors adore a dinner. Work the room and you'll overhear all sorts of scandals.
Here's a Donor List. A better list works the room faster.

lines.player: And what do I do with scandals?

lines: Spin them at the Press Podium. Raw, they're a liability. Spun, they're lunch.
Oh, and every so often a whale pledges a fortune. Smile and nod, darling. Smile and nod. And if a guest has no ears, don't mention it. They tip beautifully.
You got the list! But now HIM. The Plus-One. He's crashed every party since the Lockdown. Darling, HOW? The gates are SEALED. Somebody lets him in.
Bouncers bounce off him. Bullets bounce off him. I threw a canapé at him. Nothing.

lines.player: So how do I get him out?

lines: Darling, nothing clears a dance floor like a fireworks show. Something that goes boom on impact. Load it with Hash, darling.
Darling, the disco ball is still spinning. The Power Cell is yours. Whatever Morelight's building, it had better have a dance floor.
Between us: the donors had been hoarding that Cell for years. A lobbyist said it came out of 'an old dome, very old, don't ask'. I didn't ask. I charged corkage.
At Fundraising 20 you can work a Gala Table. At 40, the Yacht Party Deck. Bring a Rolodex, or better, a Black Book.
Juicier scandals spin into better Talking Points. Everyone wins. Except the press.
Darling, the masks were a triumph. Nobody knew who anybody was. Two guests never took theirs off. I'm no longer sure they were masks. The Power Cell is yours; Morelight says it's for 'a door'.
Between us: the donors had been hoarding that Cell for years. A lobbyist said it came out of 'an old dome, very old, don't ask'. I didn't ask. I charged corkage.
At Fundraising 20 you can work a Gala Table. At 40, the Yacht Party Deck. Bring a Rolodex, or better, a Black Book.
Juicier scandals spin into better Talking Points. Everyone wins. Except the press.
Darling, a garden party under a sealed sky. Poetic. The Power Cell is yours. Go and find a real sky, and whatever keeps flying over it at three in the morning.
Between us: the donors had been hoarding that Cell for years. A lobbyist said it came out of 'an old dome, very old, don't ask'. I didn't ask. I charged corkage.
At Fundraising 20 you can work a Gala Table. At 40, the Yacht Party Deck. Bring a Rolodex, or better, a Black Book.
Juicier scandals spin into better Talking Points. Everyone wins. Except the press.
Darling! The gala of the year. Morelight needs a Power Cell for some 'little project', and power cells are not cheap.
The donors have one. Ancient thing. They keep it in a velvet box and whisper to it. So we throw a party, the donors pay, and you, President, are the host. First things first: the theme.
Masks! Mystery! Nobody will recognize Treasurer Bickworth. Or the lobbyists' plus-ones. Perfect.
A disco ball! I already own four. Wonderful.
Outdoors, under a sealed sky. Bold. I love it.
Catering! Bring me 5 Minor Scandals for the gossip table and 3 Soundbites for the toasts.
A gala without gossip is just dinner, darling. And a dinner without gossip is just a meeting with forks.
CRASHERS! Party Crashers in my garden! And one of them stole the guest list!
Every donor, every lobbyist, and the plus-ones nobody will name. Somebody does not want that list read, darling.
Throw them out, President. Firmly. Bring me back that list.
Where's my guest list, darling? Bring it here before anyone else 'borrows' it. Or photographs it.

repeat: Darling! Back so soon? Work a Rubber Chicken Dinner with your Donor List. That is where the scandals are.
Spin them at the Press Podium. Raw, they're a liability. Spun, they're lunch.

name: Doctor Merge
examine: Can make anything sound like good news.
lines: Ah, a patient! I mean a client. I mean... the President.
A raw scandal is useless. Bring it to my podium and spin it into a Talking Point.

lines.player: What does a Talking Point do?

lines: Recite one in a fight and you feel better. It's science. Political science.
Spin badly and the story blows up in your face. Practice, President. Practice. The other side has had centuries of it.
'President Opens Door, Walks Through It.' Ninth day on the front page. I may frame it.
The Bureau's statement says 'routine maintenance'. Nobody believes it. I've never been prouder of the public.
Disaster! The Pundit has stormed the podium. He's telling everyone that 'the people' don't want a door.
Look at his ear, President. That isn't a hearing aid. Someone's feeding him lines from very, very far away.
Never argue with a pundit, President. You'll lose, even when you win.
Prove him wrong with the people. Every voice, every vote, counted. One by one.
Front page, President! 'A DOOR FOR EVERYONE.' I couldn't have written it better. I tried.
The Pundit's earpiece is in my drawer. Every hour it whispers 'stay calm, stay inside, stay tuned'. I've started taking notes.
Take the Teleprompter. Read it and you're home. And keep that press release for when you need the people.
Juicy scandals become Zingers at Spin 20. Mega scandals become Mic Drops at 40. Practice, President.
If the President vanishes, the Treasury will panic. If the President explains, the Treasury will cheer. And whoever sealed the gates will have to explain why everyone's cheering.
So: a press conference. Lorna Coinlore is waiting by the podiums. But first, practice.
Bring me 3 Soundbites. We'll warm up your voice.
Lorna Coinlore is by the podiums. Remember: never confirm, never deny, always pivot.
Optimism, President. Always optimism. And if anyone asks about aliens, smile like you know something. It drives them mad.

repeat: Back for more spin? Bring raw scandals to my podium and turn them into Talking Points.
Recite one in a fight and you feel better. Spin badly and it blows up in your face. Practice, President.

name: The Inducer
examine: Knows a guy. Is the guy. Pays people, which round here is called 'inducing'.
lines: ...You didn't see me. I'm not here. These cards aren't here either. Take them.
Lobbyists pay for favors. Hand out cards, shake hands, get paid in Tickets.
Completely. Mostly. Sometimes they find photos. Then the favor's free and you smile anyway.
Bigger lobbyists pay better, if your Lobbying is up to it. The biggest ones have clients who arrive by an elevator that only goes up. Now walk away slowly.
Word got out that the Broker signed you an Exit Permit. Now the Corporate Raider figures a President on the way out means a Treasury for sale.
Bullets? He's priced those in. He's bought every gun on the market, with fresh notes, still warm from somebody's printer. Count his fingers next time he waves.
What a thing like that can't handle is paperwork. The heavy kind, in a briefcase, swung hard. Beat him with his own filing.
He's on the east lawn, near the Broker.
You burned them. Clean hands. The Broker signed anyway; he respects that. I think it scared him. Men like him only fear one other kind of man, and they aren't from round here.
You used them. The Broker signed so fast he broke the pen. Remind me never to get on your bad side. Or on the side of whoever he reports to.
...You want out. Everyone wants out. The Lockdown Act says nobody leaves without an Exit Permit.
Only the Broker can stamp one. Nobody knows who he works for. I know who he works WITH, and you won't like them. He wants this envelope delivered first. Don't open it.
He stands by the lobbyists on the east lawn. Use the envelope on him.
A photo of you? Classic Broker. Someone took that photo, and they have the negatives.
Word is he paid the Paper-Hands, past the first barricade in the Trenches. They never hold anything for long. Go and take it off them.
You got the negatives. Hold the last frames up to the light: the Broker, shaking hands with the Corporate Raider. Seven fingers. Per hand.
Lobbyists, a Bureau, and something from upstairs. Now you've got options.
Clean. The Broker will sign; he won't want a fight. Here's your permit, and something for your trouble.
Ruthless. A lobbyist caught shaking hands with whatever that is? He'd sign anything.
He'll sign, and he'll pay. Here's your permit. Don't spend it all at once.
You again. Good. The lobbyists like you.
K Street Veterans pay better from Lobbying 20. The Shadow Brokers want 40, and they're worth it.
Keep your photos boring, President. Blackmail is bad for business. And never take a meeting in a room with no windows.

repeat: ...Still didn't see me. You've got the cards. Hand them out to the Junior Lobbyists.
Bigger lobbyists pay better, if your Lobbying is up to it. Now walk away slowly.

name: Sergeant Retain
examine: Has never once used an indoor voice. Has never once sold, either.
lines: LISTEN UP, PRESIDENT! You are soft! You are slow! You are, frankly, very well dressed!
Buy a gun at the Terminal! Every gun takes the same Rounds! Here's a stack, on the house!
Cannons fire the Hash you mine and blow up everything around the target! I LOVE CANNONS!
Pick a style in the Equipment tab: Accurate, Rapid or Longrange! Take the gun off and you swing your gavel! That's Melee!
And that dummy in the yard? SERGEANT SANDBAG! Gavels bounce right off him!
WHAT DID YOU JUST BUY AT THE TERMINAL, RECRUIT? Use it! From a distance!
Start on the Spam Bots, then the Sludgelings, then the Comment Trolls! Those Spam Bots are SURVEILLANCE, recruit! Nobody says 'gm' that much for free! DISMISSED!
AT EASE, PRESIDENT! You passed basic!
The Trenches are through the entrance on the south-east lawn! Every barricade has a boss in front of it! And SOMEBODY keeps putting them there!
Rounds run out fast! Buy them by the hundred and pack Talking Points to heal! NOW GIVE ME TWENTY!
Twenty Scrap Hash! For the budget! The printer won't fund us, so we fund ourselves! DISMISSED!

repeat: BACK AGAIN, RECRUIT? You already have your Rounds! I am not made of Rounds!
Accurate, Rapid or Longrange in the Equipment tab! Take the gun off and you swing your gavel!
And SERGEANT SANDBAG laughs at gavels! Use what you bought at the Terminal! From a distance! DISMISSED!

name: Handler Creed
examine: Covered in tiny bite marks. Proud of every one. Knows the Sproto rifleman's creed by heart.
lines: Careful, they bite. Only the ones who don't like you. So, careful.
Sprotos are little soldiers who fight beside you. Use a contract to summon one.
Loyal, blue and extremely brave. Do NOT call them gremlins.

And older than they look. They glow near old stone, they can smell a forged note at forty paces, and nobody, NOBODY, can print one. They guard the Ticket count, too: one billion, never one more. Sproto Powers, President. Officially, they don't exist.
One at a time. Specials cost Summoning points; check the Summoning tab. Here's a Recruit contract.
Your Recruit won't stop talking about you. Well. Squeaking. Every night at 3:33 it squeaks at the sky, right when the racks ping. They're arguing with something up there.
Medics at Summoning 10, Grunts at 20, Snipers at 30, Heavies at 45. Contracts are on the Terminal.
Watch your Summoning points. A special at the right moment wins fights.

repeat: Your contract's in your pack. Summon your Sproto with it; they're shy until you do.
One at a time. Specials cost Summoning points; check the Summoning tab.

name: Foreman Hallows
examine: Has a pencil behind each ear.
lines: Every President needs a bunker. Somewhere to hide when the Monetary Weather turns.
Right under this hall. I'll need materials: 10 Scrap Hash and 2 Soundbites.
Morale. My crew won't dig without a good speech. Not down there. The ground under this hall isn't soil, President. It's mud. Old mud. Flood mud. Bring both and the hatch is yours.
Bad news. Inspector Greysuit heard about the dig. He's standing on the hatch with a clipboard.
Nobody called him. His badge just says 'Bureau'. Bureau of what, I asked. He wrote me up for asking.
Not with anything fancy. Upgraded, modified, imported: he writes it up and ignores it.
He only respects regulation kit. Standard issue. The plain, boring thing they hand you on the campaign trail.
Make him sign off, President, and the hatch is yours.
Blueprints? For the Chamber? I found these twenty feet down, under the mud, in a room with the night sky painted on the ceiling. Thought they were a pizza menu.
Here. Take them to the Chamber and follow along. Don't touch the red lever. Or do. I'm not your boss.
Chamber lit up yet? If it plays music, somebody pulled the red lever. If it plays music in a key that doesn't exist, that's Tartarian. Leave it.
Heard the Chamber works. And to think I nearly ordered a pizza off those blueprints.
I've read the rest of them. The people who drew these didn't need wires. They pulled power out of the air. No wonder somebody buried them.
Inspector Greysuit signed off. The hatch is yours, President. Climb down any time.
Build spots are marked down there. Click one to see what you can build.
Bigger builds need a Pro or Elite Toolkit, plus Concrete, Steel Beams and Circuit Boards from the Terminal.
A floor. Under your floor. Marble, twenty feet down, with doorways for people twice our height. And old papers: drawings of some big machine. Probably nothing. I'll hang on to them.

name: Scout Greenhill
examine: Lookout for Expedition One. Has been in the Trenches longer than the Trenches.
lines: Welcome to the Trenches. Mind the craters.
Scout Greenhill. I was the lookout for Expedition One.
Twelve of us went north on the first day of the Lockdown. I'm the one who came back down.
Went home. Gave up. Got lost. Got visited. One of them is still up there, if you listen at night.
We dug them along the inside of the wall, heading for the north end. Took us a week.
Since then the Treasury's been tipping its worst down here. Panic. Doubt. People who sell at the first sign of trouble. And something black and wet that smells like a print shop.
It gets nastier the further north you go. Each barricade opens once you beat whatever stands in front of it.
The new maps call it a Teleport Chamber. Out of service. The old maps call it something else, and draw a star around it.
I heard it hum once. Just once. That's why I'm still here.
If you go down, your pack stays where you fell. Come back for it quick.
And Talking Points. Never leave the Treasury without them. And don't trust anyone in a grey suit. Nobody down here owns one.
I heard it from all the way down here. The hum. Then a big bang. Then nothing.
You made it out. Expedition One made it out. Took us long enough.
Soon. Somebody has to walk the Captain through. He's not used to going slowly. And I want a good look at those domes first. From cover.
The stones went quiet. Go on, President. Someone should get to see it. The real sky.
Morelight's really doing it? Waking the Chamber?
Careful up there. The old gate stones by the Chamber stood up last night. They keep saying 'NOBODY LEAVES'. Same voice as the Wrong-Namers' megaphones.
The Captain says bullets just bounce off. He says what that thing fears is a big, loud No.
Go on up. I'll keep the Trenches quiet behind you.
The Captain's still sitting by the Chamber. First time I've seen him sit.

He told me about the grey suits. Two of them, the first night. Said the Chamber was 'decommissioned by order', and if anyone found out otherwise there'd be 'consequences for the money supply'. What does that even mean?
Morelight says it needs four parts. I'll keep the Captain company. Somebody has to stop him getting up.
You stopped him. I heard it. The running. It stopped.
He's sitting by the Chamber now, catching his breath. Says he'll be first in line if it ever wakes up.
Tell Morelight what he told you. And President... thank you.
So it's the Captain's turn.
He was our leader. Best runner in the Treasury. We reached the north end in a week, and there it was: the Chamber. Cold. Dead. Built from stone nobody could name.

That night two men in grey suits walked up the Trench. We never heard them come down it. They talked to the Captain for an hour. In the morning he said: 'Keep moving. Momentum is everything.' He's been running laps in front of it ever since.
So nobody else looks at it. So nobody else asks questions. I think that's what they told him to tell himself.
He moves twice as fast as anyone. Up close, he's gone before you swing. Don't chase him.
Catch him from across the trench, mid-lap. You need reach. Real reach.
Then stop him, President. Gently, if you can. Then let's bring him home.
Quiet up there. Quieter than it's been in a year. Thank you.
I found a crate of spare megaphones behind their barricade. Stamped 'PROPERTY OF THE BUREAU. DO NOT RETURN.'
Only the Captain left now. Morelight will want to talk to you about him.
The shouting stopped mid-word. Go tell Morelight before they find a new megaphone. They seem to get them delivered.
Wrong-Namers everywhere between here and the second barricade. My ears are still ringing.
They weren't always like this. Some of them were Treasury clerks. Got scared of the walls, then somebody handed them megaphones and a script. The same script. Every one.
Their Chief guards the second barricade. Shoot at him and he just shouts louder.
Somebody needs to call that man to order, President. You've got a gavel. Use it.
The first barricade's open. First time in four hundred days. I counted.
Past it, more Trenches, and the Wrong-Namers' Chief. He'll tell you there's nothing out there. Don't listen. He's the one who read the map.
That was HER? Go tell Morelight the first barricade's open. I'm starting a new tally.
Morelight sent you? Good. I was running out of patience and snacks.
Twelve of us dug these Trenches to reach the old building on the map. Then the panic of the Lockdown came down after us and pooled up. That's her. The Sludge Mother.
Panic, and something else. Ink. Fresh money-printer ink, by the gallon. Somebody's still printing, President, and they dump the runoff down here.
She squats at the first barricade, straight north. When she's hurt she calls up Sludgelings.
Bullets go straight through her. Plop. One little hole, and she just closes it up.
You want something that hits her everywhere at once, up close. And she can't stand a party. All that panic, she hates anything cheerful.
More Trenches. And past those, the Captain. Still running. I can hear him some nights.

name: Lorna Coinlore
examine: Treasury Times, live. Always live. Keeps the archive of everything the Treasury would rather forget.
lines: Treasury Times, live. No comment? Everyone has a comment.
Since the Lockdown, the news is the only thing that gets around. That, and the grey envelopes.
Treasury Times, special edition! THE DOOR IS OPEN. The queue starts at the Trenches. Bring snacks.
Page two: DOMES SIGHTED ON HORIZON. Bureau says 'weather balloons'.
President, a word for the people who stayed?
'The door works both ways.' Front page. Again.
President! Big news? Hand it over. Use the press release on me and I'll read it live, before anyone can stop the presses.
We're still live, and the Pundit just took my microphone! He says the voters are on his side.
Funny. Nobody's ever seen him in the canteen where we vote. If only someone could actually count them.
President! Any plans to leave the Treasury? ...Off the record?

lines.player: Off the record: watch the north end of the Trenches.

lines: I KNEW it. Is it the old building? The star-shaped one on the map? I'll keep it quiet. Mostly.
We're live! President, first question: is it true the Treasury bought the wrong coin?
Honesty! In politics! I need to sit down.
(Somewhere, Doctor Merge faints. Try again.)

options.text: We didn't buy the wrong coin. We bought the wrong coin early.
lines: ...That's going on the front page. Next question!
I'll... print that, I guess. Assuming anyone's still allowed to print anything. Let's try again.
Second question: our sources say someone, somewhere, is printing money by the truckload. So why can't the Treasury just sell its Tickets and buy some?
Ouch. That's a headline you don't want. Try again.

options.text: Because selling would crash the coin and the country. So we took a Vow.
lines: A vow! The people love a vow. And nobody can print a vow. Last question!

options.text: Because the sell button is broken.
lines: Is it? ...It is, isn't it. Try again.
Final question: rumor says you're planning to leave the Treasury, to go looking for some lost civilization. Is that true?
'No comment' is a comment, President. Try again.
Noted. Bitterly. Try again.

options.text: Leave? I'm opening a door. For everyone.
lines: A door for everyone. The Treasury is going to love that. Certain people upstairs are going to hate it. That's a wrap!
That's a wrap. You were... surprisingly good. Go see Doctor Merge.
And President? The Pundit's earpiece kept talking after he went down. Not in English.

name: Morelight
examine: Chief of Staff. Somehow already here.
lines: ...We made it. Look at that, President. No walls.
Somewhere new. The coordinates only got us this far. But look across the lake: spires, domes, star-shaped walls. Tartaria, President. Standing. And somebody over there is doing magic in it.
There's a rowboat at the water's edge with a note on it. It says 'TO THE ACADEMY. ROW YOURSELF.'
The trail west goes to my ranch, by the way. I do a show on Sundays. And the road east goes to the Hatchery. Busy people, out here.
The Chamber works both ways, so go home whenever you like.
I'm going to stand here a while. Guarding the mustache. From a much better view. Counting the lights in the sky that aren't stars.
A wizard academy, inside a Tartarian star fort. Of course. And of course its treasurer was wiring the gold to the same people who sealed ours.
Some things are the same everywhere, President. The Bureau has branch offices. Good to know we're useful out here too.
Scout Greenhill brought the Captain through while you were at school. He walked the whole way. He won't stop telling people.
Two treasuries saved. Which leaves the RoadMap: one arrow, pointing up. The signpost says the rest is unexplored. I say that's the same thing.
And tune in Sunday. The Sproto Ranch is just down the west trail. We're going to tell the people everything.

name: Archmage Hodlwyn
examine: Headmaster of Moonward Academy. His beard has its own beard.
lines: Welcome to Moonward, President. Mind the students; they duel in the halls. The halls were here long before any of us.
The rug is unraveled and the gold is back in the vault. Moonward is open again, and every student wants your autograph.
We found the Bursar's ledger in the rug's lining. Every payment went three ways: a Bureau, a lobbying firm, and a set of coordinates in the night sky.
Now we teach. And you keep exploring, President. The world out here is bigger than either of us thought, and older than anyone is allowed to say.
Come back any time. Staffwright Kundalina will keep your COOM topped up.
Visitors! In a rowboat! Welcome to the Moonward Academy of Applied Wizardry. I am Archmage Hodlwyn, headmaster.
A President, from behind the big wall? Then you know locked doors, and treasuries. We've lost ours.
The crystal ball showed me your Chamber waking. I left a boat. The oars are on loan; we have a budget crisis.

lines.player: These walls are shaped like a star.

lines: Tartarian, yes. The founders didn't build Moonward; they found it. The towers drink power from the air. That's all magic is, President: old engineering nobody's allowed to patent.
Our Bursar wove the whole endowment into one magnificent rug. Then he pulled it.
Right out from under us. He calls himself the Rugmancer now, and he's spellbound our Battlemages to keep everyone out. Two gentlemen in grey robes visited him first. We don't issue grey robes.
First, you'll want to cast. Here: an Apprentice Staff, and some COOM to fire from it.
Concentrated Occult Output Matter. Little white vials. Every staff runs on it. We do not discuss where it comes from.
Wield the staff and put the COOM in your ammo slot. It fires like any gun you've held, and your Shooting carries over.
Good grip! Now practice. The Dueling Grounds are in the east wing. The Apprentices there will duel anyone who stands still.
Win one duel. Keep your distance; a staff outranges any pistol.
Splendid! Now a Battlemage. They were our best teachers before the Rugmancer's spell.
Two of them guard the way to the north tower, and more patrol the Dueling Grounds. Beat one and the spell on it breaks. Mind their bolts; they hit hard.

lines.player: The Battlemage woke up and said the spell comes from the north tower.

lines: Of course it does. The north tower is the old antenna. Tartarian. He's been using it to beam the gold's whereabouts to someone up there. Unobstructed. Unaudited.
Go up and take back the endowment. He'll call Apprentices to defend him. Spellbound ones. Go easy on them; they're only students.
Ordinary spells just get woven into his rug. It's spun from doubt, President. Every gloomy forecast since he took the gold.
Only hope unravels doubt. Ask Staffwright Kundalina for the staff that runs on it. Not the moon one. Hope.

name: Staffwright Kundalina
examine: Makes staffs. Sells COOM. Asks no questions.
lines: Staffs! Hats! Robes! COOM by the crate!
My stall's right here. Trade at the stall, not with me. I'm busy.

lines.player: What's the difference between the staffs?

lines: Bigger crystal, bigger bang. You'll need more Shooting for the good ones.
And always carry spare COOM. Nothing sadder than a wizard hitting someone with a stick.
Going after the Rugmancer? You want hope in your hands. Not the Moonward Staff; staring at the moon isn't hoping.
Twenty-five Shooting and it's yours. It's on the stall.
The President who unraveled the Rugmancer! For you, the good COOM. It's the same COOM. Same price, too.
Business is booming now the gold's back. Everyone wants a staff. Nobody asks why the crystals hum when the lights fly over.

name: Unascended Student
examine: A mature student. Third attempt at the same degree.
lines: Are you the President from behind the wall? Can I have your autograph? On my thesis?
Nobody's taught a class since the Rugmancer took the gold. We just duel. And read. My thesis is on mud-floods. My supervisor calls it 'career-limiting'.
Classes start again tomorrow! Real ones! With teachers who aren't spellbound!
Professor Ironguide says he'll make an example of the first student who duels in the library. It's going to be me.
You're going up the tower? Can you bring back my scholarship? It's woven in near the left corner of the rug.

name: Professor Ironguide
examine: Taught battle magic for forty years. Now teaches it to anyone who stands still.
lines: Ah, a new student. Of a sort. Halt, the academy is clo... no. No. I am fighting it.
Rule one: keep your distance. Apprentices can't hit what they can't reach.
Rule two: Accurate, Rapid or Longrange, same as your guns. Longrange trains Defense as well.
Rule three: COOM in the ammo slot. You'd be amazed how many forget rule three.
The spell is gone from my head. Like waking from a very long lecture. Thank you, President.
I remember a grey robe and a voice: 'keep them out of the tower'. After that, only rule one, rule two and rule three.
If you want to keep your casting sharp, the Apprentices still duel all day. Teach them some manners.

name: Captain Motion
examine: Expedition One's Captain. Sitting down. It's harder than it looks.
lines: Sitting. It's harder than it looks.
Eleven people believed me, and I ran laps so they would never look too closely. Two grey suits told me to. Said the money supply depended on it. Don't run for people like that, President.
Somebody had to be first in line if it ever woke up. I just thought it would be me.
Scout Greenhill says I walk through next. Walk. Slowly. Like a normal person.
Go on ahead, President. I have four hundred days of sitting to catch up on.
The Chamber, waking up? After all those laps?
The stones out there won't listen to bullets. I tried. For a year. A law needs a big, loud No. And that law was never ours.

name: Morelight
examine: Chief of Staff, ranch owner and Sunday-night broadcaster. Wearing a cowboy hat over the mustache's objections.
lines: Welcome to the Sproto Ranch, President. Hat on, boots muddy, cameras rolling.
Every Sunday we go live from right here. No script, no sponsors, no Bureau. Just the truth and a lot of small blue animals.
RIP MORELIGHT THE GRIZZ BEAR EATED HIM. That's the headline the Bureau had ready to print. Pre-written. I found the press release inside the bear.
FAKE NEWS. Live, on air, in front of every Sproto on the Ranch. Ratings have never been better.

And did you see them glow when you summoned? There's Tartarian stone under the corral. The Sprotos were made to guard it, President. That's the Sproto Power nobody's allowed to mention: they can't be printed, faked or bought, and they know exactly who can.
Next stop: the Hatchery, down the east road from the Chamber. Every new coin there is paired with Tickets, so the Printer's people get nothing. Which is how you know it's working.
President! Welcome to the Sproto Ranch. My ranch, my corral, and every Sunday, my show.

It's live, it's unfiltered, and it's the only broadcast out here the Bureau doesn't own. Tonight we tell the people the truth about the money: who prints it, where it goes, and why there's a dome under my barn.

lines.player: What do I need to do?

lines: Ranch rules for guests. Wear a hat. Take a slug of moonshine. Say the words. Then we let the Sprotos out.
Hat first. Any hat; put it on fresh for the camera. The camera adds ten pounds and the Bureau adds a satellite. A brim helps with both.
Lovely hat. Now: moonshine. The Ranch's finest.
It's a Hopium Soda in a jug. Don't tell the viewers. Bring me one; Staffwright Kundalina sells them across the lake, and so does the Terminal back home.
*glug* Smooth. Tastes like tomorrow. We're live in three, two...
Good evening, Ranch! Welcome to the Sproto Ranch Show. My guest tonight: the President, who has seen the domes with their own eyes. President, say the words.
Quieter than a tax return. The Sprotos are asleep. Again, with feeling.
THAT'S the words! Look at the chat. Look at the Sprotos. Look at the Bureau's satellite, quietly changing orbit.
Always, President. By us, for once. Try again.
The viewers loved it. Now, the real show. Summon a Sproto. Out here, on the old stone, you'll see what they can really do.
Officially they're a security detail. Unofficially, they're the last guardians of Tartaria, and they glow when they're home.
Look at it glow! That, folks, is Sproto Power. Unprintable. Uncounterfeitable. Very small.
And... oh dear. There's a bear in the corral. A very upright bear. With a zip.
That's The Grizz. The Bureau's been trying to make 'Morelight eaten by bear' happen for months. They've already written the headline.

Bullets won't bother it; it was issued to ignore them. Hit it with something powered by a grudge: the Gremlin Blaster from the Terminal. Or the Archmage's staff, if Hodlwyn lent you his. Tartarian air goes straight through a zip.

name: Dev Yolk
examine: Built a launchpad in a weekend and hasn't slept since. Every coin that hatches here is paired with Tickets.
lines: Welcome to the Hatchery. Every coin that hatches here is paired with Tickets. No exceptions, no backdoors, no Bureau.
Come back when you're ready to launch something.
Your coin's live, President, and every trade feeds Tickets instead of the sky.
Here's what they'll never say on the news: new money doesn't have to be printed upstairs. It can be hatched, down here, by people. Paired with Tickets, the one currency the Printer can't touch.

Returned to sender. His people pay no fees here and take none. They say ten Tickets trade for one Verse, somewhere past the edge of the map. Down here, nobody can print either. Come back any time; there's always another egg.
You must be the President. Morelight said you'd come. Welcome to the Hatchery: the launchpad where every coin is paired with Tickets.
Because everywhere else, new coins are printed out of thin air and the fees float off to whoever owns the Printer. Lobbyists. A Bureau. And a client upstairs with very large eyes.
Here, every coin is paired with Tickets, and the fees go back into Tickets. Nothing leaves the planet. The Printer hates it.
We set up shop in an old star fort. The incubators were already here. Tartarian. Warm to the touch, no power cable. Don't ask.
Let's hatch you a coin. Bring me 10 Scrap Hash to mint it, and 2 Zingers. A ticker without a joke never hatches.
The mint's warming up. Now, the important part: the name.
Bold. The domes approve.
The little blue ones will be insufferable about it. Perfect.
Ha! Now the Bureau has to report on it. In its own newsletter.
Named and minted. Now pair it: sell something at the Hatchery's Trading Terminal and the incubator matches it with Tickets. That's the handshake.
Every sale here buys a few Tickets back. That's the whole trick. The Printer can't print it, so it can't print around us.
Uh-oh. Rug Pullers on the launchpad. They follow every new coin around, trying to yank the floor out from under it.
Chase one off before your coin's first candle.
And there he is. The Extractor. Grey suit, grey face, very large eyes, and a business card from a launchpad that doesn't exist.
He skims the fees off every launch and beams them up. Calls it a 'platform cost'. The platform is in orbit.

Bullets slide off him like he's paid to ignore them. But he can't extract from hands that won't let go: the Diamond Hands Minigun. Or talk him into the ground with a Filibuster Mace. His people have no concept of a filibuster.
He hires Rug Pullers by the minute when he's losing. Don't let them pile up.
